# Optimizing the sum of own depth and exact pair depth still loses OC

This is an exact obstruction to separating the middle and endpoint
directional infima, even when their two depth functions are evaluated at
the same optimized point. It strengthens a failure of reflection
retention: the endpoint contribution here is its **exact** two-layer
depth, with every oblique tilt already optimized. It is not an OC
counterexample.

## 1. Actual compatible fibers in every continuous dimension at least two

Fix an integer d>=2 and 0<epsilon<=1/10. Let

    T={x in R^d:x_i>=0, sum_i x_i<=1},
    V=|T|=1/d!,  a=epsilon^d,
    A=epsilon T, K=T, R=T,
    r=(1+epsilon)/2, D=(A+R)/2=rT.

Lift A,K,R to integer bases -1,0,1 and take their convex hull C.
This is a full-dimensional compact convex body. The endpoint sections
are exactly A and R. A convex combination at base zero uses equal
weights on the two endpoints; its endpoint contribution lies in
D subset T. Consequently the actual middle section is exactly K=T.
The projection is [-1,1], so there are precisely these three nonempty
integer fibers. Their total mixed volume is

    M=(2+a)V.

All three fibers are positive and each has volume strictly less than
M/2. Thus neither null fibers nor a heavy-fiber shortcut is involved.

For g in T let f(g) be the ordinary raw halfspace depth in T. Let P(g)
be raw depth at the real middle point (0,g) for the measure consisting
of the two endpoint fibers alone. Equivalently, P(g) is the infimum
over every closed ambient halfspace containing (0,g), measured only
on ({-1} times A) union ({1} times R). The exact endpoint halfspace-
discrepancy formula in
`candidate e18e6db2f3e079d5` can be
used to evaluate P; it is not necessary for this certificate.

The lower bound

    depth_S(0,g)>=f(g)+P(g)

is valid. For any one ambient containing cap, its middle contribution
is at least f(g) and its endpoint contribution is at least P(g).
The following shows that even optimizing this valid lower bound over
every actual middle point cannot reach OC.

## 2. Exact maximum of the separated lower bound

One always has

    0<=P(g)<=aV.                                      (1)

Indeed the purely integer halfspace z<=0 contains (0,g) and takes
exactly the left endpoint from the endpoint-only measure.

Moreover P(g)=0 for g outside or on the boundary of D. For g outside
D, strict separation supplies a vector u with

    2u.g>h_A(u)+h_R(u).

Choose positive eta_A,eta_R summing to this strict gap. Thresholds
t_A=h_A(u)+eta_A and t_R=h_R(u)+eta_R have average u.g and
therefore are exactly the endpoint traces of one ambient halfspace
through (0,g). Both endpoint traces are empty. On the boundary of D
use a support vector u and t_A=h_A(u), t_R=h_R(u). Both traces are
support faces of full-dimensional convex bodies, hence have zero
d-volume. This proves the assertion for closed caps as well.

For g in D the particular middle cap

    {x:sum_i x_i<=sum_i g_i}

has volume (sum_i g_i)^d V, because 0<=sum_i g_i<=r<1.
Thus (1) gives

    f(g)+P(g)<= (r^d+epsilon^d)V
                <=[(11/20)^2+(1/10)^2]V
                =(5/16)V.                            (2)

Let Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d. The binomial estimate

    (1+1/d)^d < sum_(j=0)^infinity 1/j! < 3

shows Gamma_d>1/3>5/16. For the last strict series estimate, use
1/j!<=1/2^(j-1) for j>=2, with a strict inequality when j>=3.
Therefore every g in D gives a value strictly smaller than
Gamma_d V.

For all g in T, f(g)<=Gamma_d V. To see the upper bound directly,
let lambda_0,...,lambda_d be simplex barycentric coordinates. One of
the coordinates lambda_i(g) is at least 1/(d+1). The cap
lambda_i>=lambda_i(g) has volume
(1-lambda_i(g))^d V<=Gamma_d V.
At the ordinary simplex centroid

    g_T=(1/(d+1),...,1/(d+1)),

ordinary Grünbaum gives f(g_T)=Gamma_d V, with the matching
canonical cap just described. Since

    sum_i (g_T)_i=d/(d+1)>=2/3>11/20>=r,

this centroid is outside D. Hence P(g_T)=0. Outside D, P=0 and
the preceding ordinary upper bound applies. Together with (2) this
proves the exact optimization identity

    max_(g in T) [f(g)+P(g)] = Gamma_d V.              (3)

In contrast, the required OC raw target for this actual source is

    (Gamma_d/2) M=Gamma_d(1+a/2)V>Gamma_d V.           (4)

Endpoint selection does not repair this certificate. At an exposed
endpoint base, an arbitrarily tilted finite ambient cap can isolate
any chosen own-fiber cap from the other bounded fibers. Hence the
endpoint maximum raw depths are exactly Gamma_d aV and Gamma_d V.
Both are bounded by (3).

## 3. An exact planar calibration and the surviving directional formula

With d=2 and epsilon=1/10 all vertices are rational. Here

    V=1/2, M=201/200,
    max_g[f(g)+P(g)]=2/9,
    (Gamma_2/2)M=67/300,
    67/300-2/9=1/900>0.                               (5)

The source itself is OC-safe. The audited theorem
`candidate 1d1be0b22c707856` applies:
the relative endpoint mass 1/100 is less than
rho_2=2(sqrt(10)-3)/9. This inequality is exact, since it is
equivalent to sqrt(10)>609/200 and
(609/200)^2=370881/40000<10. That theorem gives actual global raw
depth

    (Gamma_2+1/100)V=409/1800,

which exceeds (4) by 7/1800. The use of this prior theorem only
certifies a safe center for the example; Sections 1--2 already
prove the obstruction independently.

The information that (3) discards is the common continuous normal.
For a unit vector u put

    F_u(g)=|T intersect {u.x>=u.g}|,
    P_u(g)=inf_t [|A intersect {u.x>=u.g+t}|
                          +|R intersect {u.x>=u.g-t}|].

Then the exact middle depth is

    min{V+aV, V+V, inf_(|u|=1)[F_u(g)+P_u(g)]}.       (6)

The first two entries retain purely integer closed caps, including
their complete middle boundary fiber. Formula (6) is not equal in
general to inf_u F_u(g)+inf_u P_u(g). The source above proves that
this distinction can be decisive even after optimizing g over the
entire actual middle fiber. Any successful deficit comparison for
this family must retain directional compatibility, rather than
charging the worst endpoint loss to every middle cap.
